name: Squad.so
tagline: A shared workspace for product teams to line up goals, opportunities and what actually ships next.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Squad has repositioned more than once, so treat plan names and tiers here as unknown until checked live.

verdictSummary: The visible surface is a structured list of goals, opportunities and roadmap items with some AI drafting on top, and that is a well trodden CRUD app an agent can produce in a weekend. Where it gets expensive is everything around the list: multiplayer editing, comment threads, permissions, Jira and Linear sync, and the Slack nagging that makes anyone actually update their items. For one person tracking their own product thinking, a local version is genuinely fine and arguably faster. For a team of six, you will rebuild account plumbing and integrations for a month and still lose. Verdict leans kinda mostly because the honest answer depends on whether you are replacing a tool or replacing a team habit.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you write goals, hang opportunities and roadmap items off them, drag them across now/next/later, and ask an LLM to draft user stories from any item.
requirements: Node 20 and a local SQLite file
An LLM API key in .env if you want the story drafting
Somewhere to run it if you want access from more than one machine
whatYouLose: Realtime multiplayer, presence and comment threads, which is most of why a team tool exists
Two way sync with Jira, Linear or GitHub, so your roadmap drifts from the actual backlog
Slack and email nudges that force stale items to get updated
Permissions, invites and an audit trail for anyone outside your own laptop
Mobile access and the polish of a product someone iterated on with real teams
moatNotes: The artifact is trivial; the shared ritual of keeping it current is not. That ritual is enforced by notifications and integrations, which is exactly the boring part you will not one-shot.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for a table of goals. They pay so that six people are looking at the same table, so the engineering tickets and the roadmap do not diverge into two competing truths, and so the person who never opens the tool gets pinged until they do. A single player clone gives you the thinking space without the enforcement, which is either the whole point or completely useless depending on why you opened the app.
notes: Fine as a personal thinking tool, weak as a team replacement; the details here are drafted from the public site and not deeply verified.
prompt:
Build a local, single user product workspace web app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js App Router with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind, server actions for all mutations. Everything runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. Data lives in ./data/workspace.db, created and migrated automatically on first boot.

Data model:
- goal: id, title, description, timeframe (quarter string), status (active | achieved | dropped), created_at
- opportunity: id, goal_id (nullable), title, notes (markdown), confidence (low | medium | high), created_at
- item: id, opportunity_id (nullable), title, body (markdown), bucket (now | next | later | shipped), effort (S | M | L), position (integer for ordering), created_at, updated_at
- story: id, item_id, text, created_at

Screens:
1. /goals: list of goals with inline create and edit, each showing its linked opportunities count.
2. /opportunities: table with filters by goal and confidence, click to open a detail drawer with markdown notes editing.
3. /roadmap: four columns (now, next, later, shipped) with drag and drop reordering that persists position and bucket. Use dnd-kit.
4. /item/[id]: full item view with body editor, parent opportunity link, and the list of generated stories.

AI drafting: one server action that takes an item id, sends its title, body and parent opportunity notes to the OpenAI chat completions API, and returns 3 to 6 user stories in the form "As a X, I want Y, so that Z", saved as story rows. Read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env.local and write a .env.example. If the key is missing, hide the button and show a one line note instead of crashing.

Also include: global keyboard shortcut cmd+k command palette for jumping to any goal, opportunity or item; a /export route that dumps the whole database as JSON; a seed script with 2 goals, 5 opportunities and 10 items so the UI is not empty.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: authentication, invites, multi user or realtime editing, comments, notifications, Jira or Linear or Slack integrations, analytics, Docker, and any hosted deployment config.

Deliver a README with setup in under ten lines, the seed command, and a short list of what was deliberately left out.
